eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 7 · Joining Financial Tables

eyebrow: Why there's a table in the middle

code:
SELECT i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount,
       c.check_number, c.check_date,
       ip.amount AS amount_on_this_check
FROM ap_invoices_all i
INNER JOIN ap_invoice_payments_all ip
    ON ip.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
INNER JOIN ap_checks_all c
    ON c.check_id = ip.check_id;
caption: Each JOIN adds one more table to the chain, each with its own ON condition.

eyebrow: What's still owed, regardless of checks
code:
SELECT i.invoice_num, ps.due_date, ps.amount_remaining
FROM ap_invoices_all i
INNER JOIN ap_payment_schedules_all ps
    ON ps.invoice_id = i.invoice_id;
caption: AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL tracks due dates and remaining balance — key to the unpaid-invoices challenge.
